numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With a NaN argument, gammainc returns finite values for some inputs. For a=NaN and x=[-inf,-1,0,1,inf,nan] it returns [nan nan 0 nan 1 nan]. For x=NaN and a=[-inf,-1,0,1,inf,nan] it returns [nan nan nan nan 0 nan]. The same behaviour appears in gammaincc, and the issue reports similar cases in chdtr and chdtrc.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Any NaN input to gammainc or gammaincc should produce NaN, so every element of both example outputs should be nan.
trigger_conditions: one argument of gammainc is NaN and the other is a finite value, zero, or an infinity
a is NaN and x is 0, 1, or inf, which returns finite values
x is NaN and a is inf, which returns 0
oracle_clues: the fix adds std::isnan checks on a and x in the igam and igamc kernels that return quiet NaN
tests were added asserting NaN for nan ar

category_specific_evidence: igam.h diff adds an early check in igam(double a, double x) returning quiet NaN when std::isnan(a) or std::isnan(x), before the x<0 or a<0 domain check
igamc (gammaincc) receives the same early NaN check returning quiet NaN when either argument is NaN
Issue #21317 reports special.gammainc(np.nan, [-inf,-1,0,1,inf,nan]) returning [nan nan 0. nan 1. nan] and gammainc(arg, np.nan) returning [nan nan nan nan 0. nan], so NaN inputs yield finite results
test_gammainc.py adds test_a_nan and test_x_nan, parametrized over -inf, -1.0, -0.0, 0.0, inf, nan, asserting np.isnan(sc.gammainc(nan, x)) and np.isnan(sc.gammainc(a, nan))
Issue #20972 and PR discussion: chdtrc(nan, x) returned [1. 1. nan nan nan nan] for x=[-inf,-1,0,1,inf,nan]; reviewer states chdtrc should return NaN for consistency with chdtr
Commit messages: add nan checks in gammainc and gammaincc scalar kernels; fix chdtrc out of domain case
reproduction_risks: dtype of inputs and outputs is not stated in the passages beyond Python/NumPy float behaviour implied by np.nan and np.inf; dtype field left null
Precision and magnitude regime are not stated; no tolerance is given because the tests use exact np.isnan assertions
Subnormals are not mentioned; signed zero appears only as the -0.0 test inputs with no stated handling beyond NaN expectation
The finite outputs at infinite arguments (0 and 1) are observed behaviour in the issue, not stated as correct values; the fix mandates NaN only for NaN inputs
The chdtrc out-of-domain fix is a separate change referenced in the same PR and is not fully specified in the passages
Environment lists OpenBLAS and NumPy 2.0.0 but these are not shown to affect the special-value handling
